scope: Staged B9 geography only. No production activation, roster closure or full-world runtime proof.
coordinateMethod: Castle pins use approximate named-site coordinates and the unchanged projection. District markers fit the unchanged outline within 40–180 world units of their parent.
districtMethod: Six prescribed province divisions and forty counties or explicit subdivisions total 2100000 koku. Resources and county assignments are gameplay design, not historical taxes or jurisdiction.
ownershipMethod: The fourteen prescribed castles aggregate Date, Ashina, Mogami, Nanbu and Ando spheres. Osaki, Yuki and Hienuki local identities remain distinct historical facts.
chronologyBoundary: Hanamaki models medieval Toyagasaki. Kozukata models the medieval earthen castle, not the 1597 Morioka construction. Later castle names do not prove 1560 buildings.
portBoundary: Tsuchizaki and Tosaminato represent canonical shipping nodes. Tosaminato's municipal archaeology dates its principal port remains to the 13th–15th centuries. Their shipping chain follows Naoetsu–Tsuchizaki–Tosaminato, not a direct Naoetsu–Tosaminato edge. Tosaminato's district marker fits the prescribed Sannohe aggregate, not the distant harbor's exact coordinates.
routeMethod: Land costs use projected distance divided by 90, rounded to 0.5 days; mountain corridors multiply by 1.5. Required grades and sea costs follow plan/14.
